event: An Israeli airstrike in Deir Qanoun an-Naher resulted in six deaths and six injuries, including two paramedics killed and three paramedics injured.

verified_facts.statement: An airstrike occurred in Deir Qanoun an-Naher, Lebanon
verified_facts.note: Location and occurrence confirmed by multiple independent sources including ICRC, WHO, and news agencies

verified_facts.statement: Six people were killed in the strike
verified_facts.note: Casualty figure reported consistently across Lebanese health ministry, international media, and humanitarian organizations

verified_facts.statement: Six people were injured in the strike
verified_facts.note: Injury figure reported consistently across sources

verified_facts.statement: Two paramedics were killed in the strike
verified_facts.note: Confirmed by Lebanese health authorities and humanitarian organizations

verified_facts.statement: Three paramedics were injured in the strike

unverified_shared_claims.statement: The strike was a 'double-tap' (second strike on first responders arriving at the scene)
unverified_shared_claims.note: Claimed by multiple framings but IDF has not confirmed this characterization; eyewitness accounts and video evidence cited by critics but not independently verified against IDF operational records

unverified_shared_claims.statement: Paramedics killed were affiliated with Hezbollah or Amal-linked organizations (Risala Scouts, Islamic Health Committee)
unverified_shared_claims.note: Asserted by counterterrorism and Hezbollah responsibility framings; organizational affiliations are documented but the operational/combatant status of individual paramedics remains disputed

unverified_shared_claims.statement: IDF identified armed Hezbollah fighters on motorcycles as the intended target
unverified_shared_claims.note: IDF claim; no independent verification of target identification or presence of armed fighters at time of strike

unverified_shared_claims.statement: Hezbollah systematically uses ambulances and paramedic uniforms for weapons transport
unverified_shared_claims.note: Claimed by Israel and counterterrorism framing; not independently verified; disputed by humanitarian organizations

unverified_shared_claims.statement: A Trump-brokered ceasefire was nominally active at the time of the strike
unverified_shared_claims.note: Ceasefire status and terms are contested; multiple sources describe ceasefire as 'fragile,' 'repeatedly violated,' or 'collapsed,' but exact status at time of this specific strike is unclear

points_of_disagreement: Whether the strike was intentionally targeting paramedics/first responders (war crime framing) vs. targeting armed Hezbollah fighters with paramedics as unintended casualties (counterterrorism framing)
Whether paramedics' affiliation with Hezbollah/Amal-linked organizations forfeits their IHL protection as medical personnel
Whether this strike is an isolated incident or part of a systematic campaign to destroy Lebanon's healthcare capacity
Whether Hezbollah's alleged misuse of ambulances and medical cover justifies strikes on paramedics and healthcare infrastructure
Whether a ceasefire was in effect and, if so, whether this strike violated it
Whether the primary responsibility for paramedic casualties lies with Israel (for striking) or Hezbollah (for embedding in civilian/medical infrastructure)
Whether the cumulative effect constitutes a humanitarian healthcare emergency requiring immediate international intervention
The credibility and reliability of IDF targeting claims vs. eyewitness and video documentation
shared_foundation.summary: All framings agree that an airstrike in Deir Qanoun an-Naher killed six people (including two paramedics) and injured six (including three paramedics). The fundamental disagreement is whether the strike targeted armed combatants with paramedics as incidental casualties, deliberately targeted first responders as a war crime, or represents part of a systematic campaign against healthcare—and whether Hezbollah's alleged misuse of medical infrastructure affects the legal and moral calculus.

framings.name: War Crimes / IHL Violation
framings.question: Did Israel's strike on responding paramedics constitute a war crime under international humanitarian law?
framings.key_claim: The killing of paramedics in a double-tap strike on first responders is a deliberate violation of IHL protections afforded to medical personnel and constitutes a war crime.
framings.description: This framing centers on whether the strike, specifically its pattern as a double-tap that hit rescuers responding to a prior attack, violates the Geneva Conventions' absolute protections for medical workers. It invokes binding IHL rules and calls for accountability or investigation.
framings.emphasizes: The protected status of paramedics under IHL, the double-tap mechanics of the strike, the absence of evidence that the responders were combatants, and the cumulative toll on Lebanon's health system.
framings.downplays: Israel's stated military rationale, the affiliations of the paramedic organizations with Hezbollah-linked bodies, and the broader Hezbollah-Israel conflict context that preceded the strike.
sample_headlines: Israel must halt attacks on healthcare workers, medical facilities and first responders — Amnesty International
Israeli strikes kill six Lebanese medics in 24 hours, health ministry says — condemning the attacks as violations of international law

carriers.name: Amnesty International
carriers.excerpt: "Deliberately striking medics performing their humanitarian functions is a serious violation of international humanitarian law and could constitute a war crime."
carriers.role_evidence: Amnesty published early, detailed legal analysis framing the pattern of strikes as apparent war crimes, coining the 'deadly playbook' characterization.

carriers.name: Lebanon Ministry of Health
carriers.excerpt: "Six Lebanese paramedics have been killed in two Israeli strikes... condemning the attacks as violations of international law."
carriers.role_evidence: The Lebanese health ministry formally condemned both strikes as IHL violations on the day of the Deir Qanoun incident, providing official institutional framing.

carriers.name: World Health Organization (Dr. Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus)
carriers.excerpt: "Attacks on health facilities must cease immediately. This cannot become the norm."
carriers.role_evidence: WHO Director-General publicly condemned the broader pattern, lending UN institutional weight to the war crimes framing.

carriers.name: NPR
carriers.excerpt: "We found that these attacks amount to apparent war crimes... Health workers are protected under the laws of war."
carriers.role_evidence: NPR distributed Amnesty's and WHO's findings to a broad US public audience, syndicated widely across PBS/NPR affiliates.

carriers.name: Drop Site News (Katrine Dige Houmøller)
carriers.excerpt: "Israel's wanton killing of rescue workers and targeting of medical infrastructure in Lebanon has been one of this war's most brazen features."
carriers.role_evidence: On-the-ground reporting from Deir Qanoun on the day of the event, providing vivid witness detail that seeded broader pickup of the IHL framing.

carriers.name: Israel-Palestine News (repost of Drop Site News)
carriers.excerpt: "More than 120 health care workers have been killed and over 260 wounded in Israeli airstrikes across Lebanon since March 2."
carriers.role_evidence: Republished and amplified the Drop Site original, reaching an explicitly pro-accountability audience.

framings.name: Counterterrorism / Military Necessity
framings.question: Did Israel lawfully target Hezbollah combatants who were using or operating near medical infrastructure, thereby forfeiting IHL protection?
framings.key_claim: Israel struck Hezbollah fighters it identified riding motorcycles in the area; paramedic organizations in the zone are affiliated with Hezbollah-linked bodies whose misuse of medical cover forfeits IHL protection.
framings.description: This framing accepts the IDF's stated narrative: the primary targets were Hezbollah operatives, and some affiliated with Hezbollah-aligned health organizations were present. It foregrounds Hezbollah's documented exploitation of ambulances and medical cover as the causal condition for the strike.
framings.emphasizes: IDF identification of armed targets, Hezbollah's alleged systematic misuse of ambulances and paramedic uniforms, the affiliation of killed responders with Hezbollah/Amal-linked organizations, Israel's right of self-defense.
framings.downplays: The lack of independently verified evidence for Hezbollah misuse at this specific incident, civilian collateral casualties including a Syrian child, the double-tap mechanics, and the cumulative humanitarian toll.
sample_headlines: Israel Targets Hezbollah Fighters Disguised as Paramedics as Terror Group Continues to Exploit Civilian Sites — Algemeiner
IDF accuses Hezbollah of 'extensive military use' of ambulances, medical facilities — Times of Israel

carriers.name: Israel Defense Forces (IDF)
carriers.excerpt: "We warn that the military use of medical facilities and ambulances must stop immediately."
carriers.role_evidence: The IDF was the originating source of the 'Hezbollah misuses ambulances' claim, issuing repeated formal statements that became the backbone of the counterterrorism framing.

carriers.name: Algemeiner
carriers.excerpt: "Israel on Sunday night intercepted a Hezbollah operation in southern Lebanon, targeting a terrorist cell disguised as paramedics."
carriers.role_evidence: Algemeiner picked up and amplified the IDF framing directly for a pro-Israel readership ahead of mainstream adoption.

carriers.name: Times of Israel
carriers.excerpt: "The Israeli military says it struck a 'Hezbollah terror cell dressed as paramedics' in southern Lebanon."
carriers.role_evidence: Times of Israel is the highest-circulation English-language Israeli outlet and gave the IDF framing its widest Anglophone reach.

carriers.name: Jerusalem Post
carriers.excerpt: "The IDF said Monday it struck a Hezbollah cell in southern Lebanon over the weekend that was operating an ambulance while posing as paramedics."
carriers.role_evidence: Second major Israeli English outlet, with broad international readership, amplifying the same IDF framing simultaneously.

carriers.name: Haaretz
carriers.excerpt: "The Israeli army has accused Hezbollah of extensively using ambulances for military purposes... but it has not provided any evidence."
carriers.role_evidence: Israeli liberal outlet Haaretz pushed back on the IDF framing by noting the absence of evidence provided, acting as an internal critic.

framings.name: Systematic Targeting of Healthcare / War on Medicine
framings.question: Does this strike represent part of a deliberate, pattern-based campaign to destroy Lebanon's healthcare infrastructure and demoralize first responders?
framings.key_claim: The Deir Qanoun strike is not an isolated incident but part of a systematic, weeks-long Israeli campaign to eliminate Lebanon's emergency medical capacity through double- and triple-tap strikes on paramedics.
framings.description: This framing zooms out from the individual strike to identify a strategic pattern: over 120 healthcare workers killed, 139 ambulances damaged, hospitals shuttered, and rescuers targeted in sequential strikes as they respond to earlier attacks. The question it asks is whether a deliberate strategy—not collateral damage—is at work.
framings.emphasizes: The cumulative scale and frequency of strikes on medics, the double-tap strike methodology, body cam footage as documentation, the psychological toll on surviving crews, and the collapse of healthcare access in southern Lebanon.
framings.downplays: Israeli military rationale and individual targeting decisions, Hezbollah's rocket campaign, and geopolitical context of the wider Israel-Iran war.
sample_headlines: Israel Is on a Killing Spree of Paramedics and Rescue Workers in Lebanon — Drop Site News
120 killed in Israel's war on Lebanon's healthcare workers — Workers Revolutionary Party
The medics refusing to abandon south Lebanon under Israeli fire — The New Arab

carriers.name: Drop Site News
carriers.excerpt: "Rescue teams describe a pattern of repeated Israeli attacks directly targeting their members, often in double—or triple-tap strikes."
carriers.role_evidence: Drop Site News originated the 'killing spree' pattern framing with on-the-ground sourcing from Deir Qanoun on the day of the event.

carriers.name: The New Arab
carriers.excerpt: "Double-tap strikes have become a grim reality for paramedics."
carriers.role_evidence: Published immersive feature reporting on the same double-tap pattern with named paramedic sources, extending the framing to an Arab Anglophone audience.

carriers.name: Arab News
carriers.excerpt: "Rescue teams report deadly strikes, damaged ambulances, and mounting casualties as war overwhelms emergency response."
carriers.role_evidence: Arab News reached a Gulf and global Arabic diaspora audience with detailed reporting on the healthcare collapse framing.

carriers.name: PBS NewsHour
carriers.excerpt: "The three strikes... is the latest example of Israel's willingness to target Lebanon's health sector."
carriers.role_evidence: US public broadcaster amplified the pattern framing with eyewitness accounts to a mainstream American audience.

carriers.name: Middle East Eye
carriers.excerpt: "Double tap strike in southern Lebanon kills, injures paramedics."
carriers.role_evidence: Live-blogged the double-tap mechanics of the Deir Qanoun strike in real time, establishing the terminology that dominated later coverage.

framings.name: Ceasefire Collapse / Diplomatic Failure
framings.question: Does this strike demonstrate that the Trump-brokered Lebanon ceasefire is failing, and what does that mean for broader US-Israel-Iran diplomacy?
framings.key_claim: The Deir Qanoun strike is evidence that Israel is defying a nominally active Trump-brokered ceasefire, undermining US diplomatic credibility and threatening the wider Iran nuclear deal negotiations.
framings.description: This framing situates the strike within the geopolitical arc of the April 2026 Trump-announced ceasefire, asking whether Israel's continued operations—including strikes killing civilians and paramedics—constitute a de facto rejection of US-led diplomacy and what consequences that carries for Trump's leverage.
framings.emphasizes: The existence of an active ceasefire at the time of the strike, Trump's public frustration with Netanyahu, the risk of Lebanon strikes derailing US-Iran talks, the shaky and repeatedly violated nature of each ceasefire agreement.
framings.downplays: The human cost and IHL dimensions of the individual strike, Hezbollah's ongoing rocket fire, and ground-level military dynamics in southern Lebanon.
sample_headlines: Israel defies Trump's ceasefire with new strikes on Lebanon — Newsweek
Israel launches new Lebanon strikes even as Trump insists Iran deal is coming soon — NBC News

carriers.name: Newsweek
carriers.excerpt: "Israeli attacks on Lebanon come despite Trump's order to Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to halt strikes."
carriers.role_evidence: Newsweek framed continued Israeli strikes—including in the Deir Qanoun timeframe—explicitly as defiance of Trump, popularizing that angle for a US audience.

carriers.name: NBC News
carriers.excerpt: "The Israeli military launched deadly new strikes in Lebanon... despite President Donald Trump saying both sides had agreed to de-escalate."
carriers.role_evidence: Major US broadcast outlet framing Lebanon strikes—including the May 22 Deir Qanoun cluster—as a diplomatic rupture threatening the Iran deal.

carriers.name: NPR
carriers.excerpt: "These ceasefires between Israel and Hezbollah essentially have been quite tenuous, and they've been broken almost on a daily basis."
carriers.role_evidence: NPR contextualized the ongoing strikes pattern as ceasefire collapse, quoting a Middle East Institute analyst to frame US diplomatic stakes.

carriers.name: CBS News
carriers.excerpt: "Trump has repeatedly suggested the two sides are close to a deal... but so far no agreement has materialized."
carriers.role_evidence: CBS live-updated the gap between Trump's peace claims and Israel's continuing strikes, including on Lebanon's paramedics and civilians.

carriers.name: President Donald Trump / White House
carriers.excerpt: "He was hit, and he hit back, and I can't blame him for that."
carriers.role_evidence: Trump's own public statements—including reported profane frustration with Netanyahu—institutionalized the framing of Israel's strikes as a diplomatic management problem for Washington.

framings.name: Human Cost / Bearing Witness
framings.question: Who are the individuals killed and injured, and what does their loss mean for communities already under sustained bombardment?
framings.key_claim: Ahmed Hariri and his colleagues were named, documented people—paramedics and community members—whose deaths amid rubble recovery illuminate the human face of a war that statistics alone cannot convey.
framings.description: This framing foregrounds the identities, stories, and grief of those killed or injured—named paramedics, a Syrian child, colleagues who worked and slept together—using on-the-ground narrative journalism and testimony to make visible what casualty numbers abstract away.
framings.emphasizes: Named victims and their personal histories, witness grief and trauma, the lived conditions of paramedics sleeping in hospitals while families evacuate, and the acts of courage shown before death.
framings.downplays: Legal and political dimensions of accountability, military rationale, or geopolitical stakes; the framing deliberately brackets the 'why' to focus on the 'who.'
sample_headlines: Witnesses detail deadly Israeli strikes on medics in Lebanon — PBS NewsHour / Associated Press
The medics refusing to abandon south Lebanon under Israeli fire — The New Arab

carriers.name: Drop Site News / Katrine Dige Houmøller
carriers.excerpt: "Ahmed Hariri, a paramedic and photojournalist was among them. Dust rose from the ruins as the men dug hurriedly for any sign of life—or death."
carriers.role_evidence: Houmøller was physically present at Deir Qanoun and was the first to document Hariri by name before and after his death, originating the personal witness framing.

carriers.name: The New Arab
carriers.excerpt: "'This is a psychological war, and the aim [of the attacks] is to create terror for the ambulance crews,' said Mohammed Suleiman."
carriers.role_evidence: Extended feature gave named responders a platform to describe their psychological and physical experience, amplifying the human cost framing.

carriers.name: Associated Press / PBS NewsHour
carriers.excerpt: "'I felt sick. I couldn't believe my eyes,' Mohammed Jaber, 43, told The Associated Press."
carriers.role_evidence: AP's wire reporting with named witnesses and graphic scene description reached the widest US and global readership via syndication.

carriers.name: Al Jazeera (video)
carriers.excerpt: "Video shows an Israeli air strike hitting paramedics responding to an earlier attack in southern Lebanon."
carriers.role_evidence: Al Jazeera's video of the live double-tap strike on paramedics became the most widely circulated visual documentation of the event globally.

framings.name: Hezbollah Responsibility / Dual-Use Shield
framings.question: Does Hezbollah's strategy of embedding military operations within civilian and medical infrastructure bear primary moral and legal responsibility for paramedic deaths?
framings.key_claim: By systematically co-opting ambulances and Hezbollah/Amal-affiliated health organizations for weapons transport and cover, Hezbollah created the conditions that led to civilian and paramedic casualties in Deir Qanoun.
framings.description: This framing shifts moral agency from Israel's trigger to Hezbollah's strategy, arguing that the 'human shield' use of medical infrastructure is itself an IHL violation that both endangers civilians and provides legal justification for Israeli action. It questions whether the struck organizations were purely humanitarian.
framings.emphasizes: The Hezbollah and Amal affiliations of the Risala Scouts and Islamic Health Committee, IDF intelligence claims about weapons transport in ambulances, Hezbollah's broader pattern of embedding in civilian infrastructure, and Lebanon's failure to disarm Hezbollah.
framings.downplays: The independent civilian functions of these health organizations, the lack of verified evidence of military misuse at this specific incident, the double-tap timing, and the Syrian child among the dead.
sample_headlines: IDF says it struck Hezbollah operatives dressed as paramedics in south Lebanon — Times of Israel
Hezbollah uses ambulances, paramedic uniforms, as disguise for terrorist activity, IDF says — Jerusalem Post

carriers.name: IDF Spokesperson Col. Avichay Adraee
carriers.excerpt: "The use of ambulances and medical teams to conceal terrorist activities constitutes a severe violation of international law."
carriers.role_evidence: IDF spokesperson statements were the originating source of the Hezbollah-shields framing, repeatedly issued across the conflict.

carriers.name: Algemeiner
carriers.excerpt: "The Israeli strike further exposed the Iran-backed Lebanese terrorist group's use of civilians and even medical vehicles as cover for attacks."
carriers.role_evidence: Algemeiner was among the first outlets to frame the IDF narrative as the primary lens, ahead of mainstream Israeli or US conservative media.

carriers.name: Naharnet
carriers.excerpt: "The association is linked with the Hezbollah-allied Amal movement."
carriers.role_evidence: Lebanese wire service Naharnet noted the organizational affiliations of the killed paramedics, providing factual detail that carries in this framing.

carriers.name: PBS NewsHour / Associated Press
carriers.excerpt: "Such attacks became a contentious issue... as Israel accused Hezbollah... of using Lebanese hospitals as cover — a claim denied by Hezbollah."
carriers.role_evidence: PBS/AP presented both sides but emphasized the contested and unverified nature of the dual-use claim, acting as a partial critic of this framing.

framings.name: Collapse of Healthcare Access / Humanitarian Emergency
framings.question: What are the downstream consequences of sustained attacks on health infrastructure for the civilian population of southern Lebanon?
framings.key_claim: The cumulative destruction of ambulances, clinics, and now the psychological deterrence of paramedics amounts to a humanitarian healthcare collapse that endangers every civilian in southern Lebanon regardless of the conflict's political dimensions.
framings.description: This framing, led by UN agencies and humanitarian organizations, foregrounds the functional collapse of emergency medicine: hospitals closing, ambulances destroyed, rescue workers deterred from responding. It asks what happens to sick and injured civilians when the health system ceases to function, and urges humanitarian access independent of political resolution.
framings.emphasizes: WHO and ICRC data on healthcare system damage, the chilling effect on surviving paramedics, hospital closures, the civilian population's inability to access emergency care, and calls for immediate protection of healthcare.
framings.downplays: Military targeting rationale, IHL adjudication, or political responsibility for the conflict's initiation.
sample_headlines: How Israeli strikes on paramedics are hindering rescue efforts in Lebanon — Arab News
Several hospitals in southern Lebanon have been damaged or entirely put out of service by Israeli strikes, according to the World Health Organization

carriers.name: World Health Organization
carriers.excerpt: "Several hospitals in southern Lebanon have been damaged or entirely put out of service by Israeli strikes, according to the World Health Organization."
carriers.role_evidence: WHO data on hospital and ambulance destruction anchored the humanitarian emergency framing across virtually all mainstream reporting on the event.

carriers.name: Arab News
carriers.excerpt: "The dangers have slowed rescue efforts, leaving victims trapped beneath rubble for days and further straining already stretched healthcare systems."
carriers.role_evidence: Arab News published detailed operational reporting on the functional consequences for rescue capacity, framing it as a humanitarian rather than purely legal or political story.

carriers.name: Aaj English TV (AFP wire)
carriers.excerpt: "International humanitarian law affords protection to frontline responders, healthcare workers and civilian infrastructure, including healthcare centres."
carriers.role_evidence: Carried the AFP wire story on the Deir Qanoun and Hanaway strikes, foregrounding the functional healthcare access consequences for a broad global audience.

carriers.name: Amnesty International
carriers.excerpt: "Healthcare workers are risking their lives to save others, and hospitals, other medical facilities and ambulances are specifically protected under international humanitarian law."
carriers.role_evidence: Amnesty layered humanitarian access concerns onto its IHL framing, lending NGO institutional authority to the healthcare collapse angle.

framings.name: Information War / Credibility Contest
framings.question: Whose account of what happened at Deir Qanoun is credible, and how are competing narratives being deployed as weapons in a broader information conflict?
framings.key_claim: Israel and its critics are each presenting incompatible accounts—the IDF says it struck Hezbollah fighters on motorcycles; Lebanon says paramedics responding to a prior strike were killed—and this credibility gap itself is a front in the conflict.
framings.description: This meta-framing examines how both sides construct and deploy competing narratives about events like Deir Qanoun. It highlights contested facts (armed fighters vs. responding paramedics), the role of video evidence, the IDF's pattern of post-hoc 'review' statements, and the media ecosystem's role in adjudicating those claims.
framings.emphasizes: The IDF's unverified claims vs. eyewitness/video evidence, the pattern of IDF investigations that rarely result in accountability, Israel's 'information war' as characterized by critics, the role of GoPro footage and body cameras as counter-evidence.
framings.downplays: Neither side's position—this framing is explicitly about the contest between positions rather than endorsing one.
sample_headlines: Israel's False Paramedics Story Exemplifies Its Information War Against Palestinians — Israel-Palestine News
Without Evidence, IDF Claims Again That Hezbollah Is Extensively Using Ambulances for Military Purposes — Haaretz

carriers.name: Haaretz
carriers.excerpt: "The Israeli army has accused Hezbollah of extensively using ambulances for military purposes... but it has not provided any evidence."
carriers.role_evidence: Haaretz was the first major outlet to explicitly examine the evidentiary gap in IDF claims, originating the 'information war' framing from within Israel.

carriers.name: Israel-Palestine News
carriers.excerpt: "Instead of denying the claims, Israel has repeatedly accused Hezbollah of using ambulances and medical facilities for military purposes, without providing any evidence to back up its claims."
carriers.role_evidence: Explicitly named the 'information war' dynamic in a headline and editorial framing, building on the Haaretz evidentiary critique.

carriers.name: Naharnet
carriers.excerpt: "The Israeli military said it killed two people who were armed and 'moving in a suspicious manner'."
carriers.role_evidence: Juxtaposed the IDF's stated justification alongside the Lebanese ministry's account without adjudicating, exposing the credibility gap implicitly.

carriers.name: US News & World Report (AFP wire)
carriers.excerpt: "The military said it was examining claims that 'several uninvolved individuals in the area, who were not the targets of the strikes, were harmed'."
carriers.role_evidence: Mainstream US outlet carrying the IDF's 'under review' hedging language alongside Lebanon's condemnation, surfacing the credibility contest for a broad American audience.

carriers.name: New Arab
carriers.excerpt: "Paramedics have started wearing body cameras to document potential war crimes – and their own deaths."
carriers.role_evidence: Highlighted the paramedics' own effort to produce counter-evidence via body cameras, framing the information war as one where the victims are now active documentary participants.

gap_analysis: Missing: the operational/tactical perspective from Israeli military command explaining specific targeting rationale, intelligence assessment, or claimed threats in that location. Missing: Lebanese state institutional response (government statements, investigations, formal complaints to international bodies) distinct from humanitarian framing. Missing: the paramedics' own professional/union perspective on workplace safety decisions and risk assessment in conflict zones. Missing: regional/sectarian dynamics—how this event is interpreted differently across Sunni, Shia, Christian, and Druze communities in Lebanon, or how it fits into broader Israel-Hezbollah escalation patterns versus isolated incidents framing.
